Electromagnetism — field around a wire & solenoid

questions.q: Which circuit symbol shows two parallel lines of unequal length, one long and thin and one short and thick?
questions.explain: A cell is drawn as a long thin line (positive terminal) and a short thick line (negative terminal). A battery is two or more cells in series.

questions.q: A current of 0.50 A flows for 120 s. Calculate the charge that flows.
A potential difference of 12 V is applied across a 4.0 ohm resistor. Calculate the current.
questions.explain: Rearranging V = I R gives I = V / R = 12 / 4.0 = 3 A.

questions.q: The I-V graph for an ohmic resistor at constant temperature is:
options: A straight line through the origin
A curve that flattens at high voltage
A line only in one direction
questions.explain: For an ohmic conductor at constant temperature, current is directly proportional to potential difference, so the I-V graph is a straight line through the origin (constant resistance).

questions.q: As light intensity falling on a light-dependent resistor (LDR) increases, its resistance:
questions.explain: An LDR's resistance decreases as light intensity increases (high resistance in the dark, low resistance in bright light). This is used in light-sensing circuits.

questions.q: Two resistors of 5.0 ohm and 10.0 ohm are connected in series. Calculate the total resistance.
questions.explain: In series, resistances add: R = R1 + R2 = 5.0 + 10.0 = 15 ohm.

questions.q: What are the frequency and potential difference of the UK mains supply?
questions.explain: The UK mains supply is alternating current (ac) at a frequency of 50 Hz and a potential difference of about 230 V.

questions.q: An appliance operates at 230 V and draws a current of 13 A. Calculate its power.
A 60 W lamp is switched on for 300 s. Calculate the energy transferred.
Why does the national grid transmit electricity at very high potential difference and low current?
options: To increase the resistance of the cables
To reduce energy wasted as heat in the cables
To make the current alternate faster
questions.explain: Power loss in cables is given by P = I^2 R, so reducing the current greatly reduces energy wasted as heat. Step-up transformers raise the p.d. and lower the current for efficient transmission.

questions.q: Two magnets are placed near each other. Which pairing will REPEL?
options: A magnet near an unmagnetised iron nail
questions.explain: Like poles repel, so two north poles push apart. Unlike poles (N–S) attract, and an unmagnetised iron nail is always attracted (induced magnetism).

questions.q: In what direction do magnetic field lines around a bar magnet point?
options: From south pole to north pole outside the magnet
From north pole to south pole outside the magnet
questions.explain: By convention, magnetic field lines travel from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet. The direction is the direction of the force on a north pole.

questions.q: What is the shape of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire?
options: A field like a bar magnet
questions.explain: A current in a straight wire produces a magnetic field of concentric circles around the wire. The field is stronger nearer the wire and with a larger current.

questions.q: The motor effect produces the LARGEST force on a current-carrying wire when the wire is...
questions.explain: The force is greatest when the wire is perpendicular (90°) to the field. When the wire is parallel to the field, the force is zero.

questions.q: Which action will induce a potential difference in a coil of wire? (generator effect)
options: Holding a stationary magnet inside the coil
Moving a magnet into or out of the coil
Placing the coil far from any magnet
Leaving the coil in a steady magnetic field
questions.explain: A potential difference is induced only when there is a change in the magnetic field through the coil, e.g. moving a magnet in or out. A stationary magnet causes no induced p.d.

questions.q: A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary coil than the primary. What does it do to the potential difference?
questions.explain: In a step-up transformer np < ns, so by Vp/Vs = np/ns the secondary (output) p.d. is greater than the primary. The current is correspondingly smaller.

questions.q: Which component is represented by a circle with a cross inside it?
questions.explain: A filament lamp is shown as a circle with a cross inside. A diode is a triangle pointing to a line, and a fuse is a rectangle with a line through it.

questions.q: A charge of 90 C flows through a wire in 30 s. Calculate the current.
questions.explain: Rearranging Q = I t gives I = Q / t = 90 / 30 = 3 A.

questions.q: A current of 0.25 A flows through a resistor when 5.0 V is applied across it. Calculate its resistance.
questions.explain: Rearranging V = I R gives R = V / I = 5.0 / 0.25 = 20 ohm.

questions.q: Why does the I-V graph for a filament lamp curve (becomes less steep) as the voltage increases?
options: Resistance increases as the filament heats up
Current is used up in the filament
The lamp acts like a diode
questions.explain: As current increases the filament gets hotter, ions vibrate more and resistance increases, so current rises less steeply - giving the characteristic curve.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a thermistor as its temperature rises?
questions.explain: For a typical (NTC) thermistor, resistance decreases as temperature increases. This is used in temperature-sensing circuits such as thermostats.

questions.q: Two identical resistors are connected in parallel. How does the total resistance compare with that of a single resistor?
questions.explain: Adding resistors in parallel provides more paths for charge to flow, so the total resistance is less than the smallest individual resistor (for two equal resistors, it is half).

questions.q: In a UK three-pin plug, what colour is the live wire?
questions.explain: The live wire is brown, the neutral wire is blue, and the earth wire is green and yellow striped. The live wire alternates between a high positive and negative potential.

questions.q: A current of 2.0 A flows through a 5.0 ohm resistor. Calculate the power dissipated.
